questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to UK, since I can speak the language. I chose Manchester specifically because of the courses they offered.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Would have been nice with an Erasmus meet-up in the beginning of the semester. Academically I was very satisfied.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay. Some of the stuff about housing took some time, but I figured it out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I don't remember receiving any.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Could have been nice with an "welcome to exchange students" evening or something like that.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was all right for me, I did write a lot of e-mails with the housing office though.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was just very overpriced, and that it was not necessarily social just because there was a shared kitchen.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The room I had was fine, also with own bathroom. But it was way over priced especially for students. There was a mouse in the kitchen that I told the people working at the dorm about, but so far as I know, they did not do anything.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I went okay. But I was unsure about a lot of stuff, so I wrote a lot of e-mails. The administrator answering the mails was very helpful and answered the e-mail quickly.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think it mostly went over e-mail - picking classes and stuff like that.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The administrator responsible for Politics was very helpful on mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful, I got the classes I wanted, and also got to change a class once I was there.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start in good time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was very similar to that of Copenhagen University. So it felt like the classes made sense for my degree.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was more active participation at University of Manchester which was very nice. The teachers generally engaged more with the students. The teachers encouraged meeting with them to talk about plans for exam papers, which was also more engaging than what I am used to from Copenhagen.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
SOCY60992 New Developments in Theories of Gender and Sexuality. 
POLI71162 Race and Capitalism.
POLI71082 Gender & Global Political Economy.
POLI60182 Governing in an Unjust World: Justice and International Relations.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend 'Gender & Global Political Economy' and 'Race and Capitalism', as they had very interesting specific lenses on Global Political Economy and really seemed like quite unique courses, at least in comparison with the courses available at Copenhagen's Politics department.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I needed glasses while I was there, so that was unexpected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than I had expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of societies and sports clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The international society and the nordic society if they are nordic.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going to Edale with the train and going for a day-hike. Going to museums in Manchester since they are free.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was all right. It helped a lot that I spoke the language.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just taking the initiative to go for a coffee or beer. And easier just join events from the international society, everybody comes there to meet people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Sometimes British people, were very bad at making plans beforehand.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are generally more open than in Denmark.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Student housing is easy but overpriced. I would recommend the courses I had. Look into the international society.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't have anything particular.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The academic part. I had some really nice courses and learned stuff, I know, I would not be able to learn at Copenhagen University.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exams were four individual essay of around nine pages that was to be handed in quite close to each other in time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
